title: First 5-day Tokyo Game Show in 30 years cuts back to 4 in face of Typhoon Dujuan
summary: The gamer's traditional enemy, the typhoon.
body: As reported by Kotaku , the organizers of the Tokyo Game Show have announced that its final day has been canceled and tickets for Monday, September 21 will be refunded. This was supposed to be the first five-day event in TGS' 30-year run⁠—while I am not a superstitious man, God or karma or something may be trying to tell us that it's just supposed to be a four-day deal. "Due to the approach of Typhoon No. 25, strong winds and rain are expected to intensify in the afternoon and beyond, and disruptions to transportation are also a concern," event organizers wrote on Twitter . "Therefore, prioritizing the safety of all attendees, exhibitors, and related parties, as well as ensuring safe return home, we have decided to cancel the event for the entire day." 【重要】台風25号接近に伴う9月20日(日)・21日(月・祝)の開催およびチケットの払い戻しについて最新の気象情報や交通機関への影響等を踏まえ慎重に検討した結果、以下の通り決定いたしましたのでお知らせいたします。■9月20日(日)：予定通り開催… September 19, 2026 The TGS showfloor will remain open for today, September 20, with potential modifications. There is no word on how the event will address publishers and devs who rented out space for the final day. summary: These must be flying fish.
body: Perhaps the most famous British meal is fish and chips. It's hard to beat a perfectly battered, crispy piece of fish, served with salty, pillowy soft chips absolutely drowned in vinegar. I'm getting hungry just thinking about it. But we're here to talk about Fish & Ships, a new co-op game about a group of fish piloting an airship in search of the ocean. title: I lost hours to this roguelike card-based city builder even though I had no idea how all of those words could fit together
summary: Boldly step into the mist and confront whatever horrors may emerge.
body: When I first heard about this card-based roguelike city builder, I was confused. Then I played a round. And another. And another. And another. And before I knew it far too much time had passed and I was absolutely hooked. That game is Toxic Frontier, and we just revealed it at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. Toxic Frontier plays on a hexagonal grid that makes it feel a bit like Settlers of Catan, only I'm not screaming at my housemates because they won't accept my very reasonable trade offers. You draw cards such as villages, forests, sheep, mountains, lakes, and more, and try to find the synergies while expanding into the titular toxic wasteland. title: Solarpunk MMO Loftia is launching into early access November 3
summary: Live on your very own island in the sky.
body: How come the future in videogames is, more often than not, dark and gloomy? Where's the hope? Where's the optimism? It's all in Loftia, an MMO life sim with a delightfully cheery, eco-friendly aesthetic. And, as was just revealed at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, you'll be able to get your hands on it November 3. For those of you not in the know, Loftia is an eco-optimism life sim MMO that's been in development for the last four years. You and other players inhabiting the world will each get your own floating island to call home, and you've got a bunch of sustainable ways to decorate and power your slice of sanctuary. Wishlist Loftia on Steam Early access release date: November 3, 2026 Build a sustainable home on a sky island and work with your community to build the third space of your dreams. Wishlist Loftia on Steam . Wishlist now You can grow crops in cute hydroponic shelves, rescue animals, and go on adventures with other people. These aren't focused on combat, and will instead feature puzzles and platforming challenges. There are also community projects that everyone can join in on, so you can live out your commune dreams. "We wanted a relaxing online world we could escape…

title: Unlock your inner Superman with a new demo from Undefeated: Genesis
summary: Fly fast, shoot lasers from your eyes. You know? Superhero stuff.
body: How cool would it be to wake up on an alien world with super powers? That's basically what happened to Superman himself. Now it's Albert Haltree's turn to fly around and save the day in Undefeated: Genesis, an action RPG with a new demo out now. Al woke up one day on the alien world of Voltissia, and, for some unknown reason, he awoke with super powers. In the new trailer debuted at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, we see Al's powers in full force. He can fly, shoot beams from his eyes, fire magical orbs from his hands, and summon a barrier that reminds me of the AT fields in Neon Genesis Evangelion. All that while in the air, too. Wishlist Undefeated: Genesis on Steam Release date: 2027 Undefeated: Genesis lets you live out the fantasy of becoming a superhero. Awaken on an alien world and fly, shoot lasers, and wield incredible powers in the new demo, out now on Steam . We also see some more animalistic opponents; one seems to be a big crab and another a gorilla or troll of some sort—Al is on an alien world, so anything is possible. All we know …

title: Marked For Mayhem is a 4-player dungeon crawler that wants you to try to win as a team while also beating all your teammates as a player—good luck
summary: I am being devoured by my own contradictions already.
body: Heads up, hotshot: you are being dispatched to a hostile alien planet. You will have to overcome life-or-death challenges that test your wits, physicality, and raw luck. You may die. You will almost certainly be hurt. Also, the whole thing is being televised. How many friends would you like to take with you? If you answered three, you're in luck—Marked For Mayhem is a four-player dungeon crawler which just got a world premiere at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, and I pretty much just gave you its elevator pitch in the opening paragraph. The aim of the game is to venture to planets that would really quite like to kill you and complete bounties, beat foes, take on bosses, and even partake in a few minigames. Wishlist Marked for Mayhem on Steam Release date: TBA Marked For Mayhem is a four-player dungeon crawler with an interesting premise: what if you had to deal with two essentially contradictory goals at once? Here, it means working with your team to overcome challenges while also competing with your teammates for the singular, individual winner position. I predict broken friendships aplenty. Sign up for the beta . Wishlist now To do that, you'll need to cooperate with your pals.…

title: Robots versus fungi FPS Mycopunk is leaving early access next month
summary: Just enough time to gather your squad and prepare to deploy.
body: Good news co-op fans, Mycopunk just revealed its 1.0 launch date at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. It's coming October 20, so you only have to wait exactly one month for it. If you're unfamiliar with Pigeons at Play's FPS, let me get you caught up. You and your friends play as a squad of robots who get sent to alien planets to kill the fungal monstrosities that are infesting everything. Neat. Each world you arrive on has a mission for you to complete. These can range from simple objectives like clearing an area of enemies, or more complex ones like building railguns to shoot down space ships. You get multiple lives per mission, so you can go solo if your friends are busy, or at least not get annoyed when they croak. body: "Oh man, can't wait to fly this plane through the fog around these spooky towers. I sure hope I don't lose my mind like the guy who did this job before me." It's a first-person horror flight sim made by Rubeki, developer of Lorn's Lure, and this is even set in the same world. title: Defend your farm from a gaze of raccoons in this charming tower defense roguelite, out tomorrow
summary: Please don't make me fight the trash pandas, I love them.
body: Never say I'm biased or I don't have an open mind, because here I am, telling you about a videogame where raccoons—my favourite animal on this Earth—are the enemy. Heartbreaking, I know. In The Rabbit Haul, the crafty little scamps are pestering a bunny named Sprout, so they decide to turn their garden into a warzone that can keep the mischievous Trash Panda Posse at bay. Why does Sprout need to keep the raccoons away? Well, they kind of destroyed the town. I'm sure they didn't mean to and were just looking for snacks. Still, one has to defend one's home, so Sprout gets to planting deadly organic weaponry during the day and fighting off the hordes of ringtails at night. Sprout gets in on the action themselves, so you won't just be passively watching your plants do all the hard work. title: We just saw a big chunk of Thief Remastered gameplay, and I'm more desperate than ever to play

body: There aren't many things I'm looking forward to more than Nightdive's remaster of the original Thief. Is this because I'm old? At the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, we got a hefty helping of gameplay in a new trailer for the remaster, showing Garrett stuffing his pockets in all manner of poorly-lit, erm, manors, plus sewers, crypts, tombs, dungeons—you know, Thief places. title: Core Keeper's Riders of the Underground update drops tomorrow, and you can get a sneak peek of it right here
summary: A new sub-biome, mounts, and more.
body: I can relate to the explorers in Core Keeper, because if I found an ancient, glowing orb, I know without a shadow of a doubt that I'd touch it, consequences be damned. Seems a lot of you feel the same way, because years after its early access release, Core Keeper is still going strong. We've just premiered a trailer for its new Riders of the Underground update, launching tomorrow, and it's a corker. The main addition, as the name of the update suggests, is rideable mounts. Every type of cattle can now be ridden into the depths. All you have to do is grab a saddle, a new item, and approach your desired mount. Once you've tamed your ride, you can change its name and decide on its behaviour—will it stay in place, follow you around, or roam aimlessly? You decide. summary: Dive back into the paper dungeon and prepare to fight a whole lotta dragons.
body: Hellcard 2, a sequel to the original Hellcard which received 'Very Positive' reviews on Steam, is getting a new co-op demo that you can dive into right now. The paper models give the game an interesting look that makes the deckbuilding aspect feel more tactile and real—the new trailer we just debuted even starts with a scene that looks like a popup book opening. title: Dust till Dawn is a horror-themed clean-'em-up with music from Silent Hill's composer
summary: Clean freaks.
body: At first glance you could be forgiven for thinking Dust till Dawn was a simple cleaning game. Early into the World Premiere trailer, showing the game off for the very first time during the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, it seems very mundane at first glance as you clean your way around a Japanese apartment, little cash amounts floating off of each item as you scrub it and put it back in place. Then, it twists and music from Akira Yamaoka, composer of the Silent Hill games, kicks in and you see the dual nature of Dust till Dawn, which is not just a cleaning game but also a horror, somehow. Don't worry though, you'll still be asked to clean to the best of your ability, even as everything goes to hell around you. Young Suns is an optimistic life sim for an unoptimistic time coming in November, and I'm already forming intense opinions about its cast of NPCs
summary: I would die for Nora. Sorry not sorry.
body: If you had to move to another planet in our solar system, which would you pick? Me, I'd go Neptune. I've always thought it's underrated, as our neighbours go, and it's a particularly pleasing shade of blue. I would die immediately due to cold and pressure, which I guess is a problem. I guess that problem is why the stars of Young Suns, which just revealed a November 3 release date at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, have elected to set themselves up on Jupiter. They're having a pretty cosy time of it, too: the game is a 1-4 player life sim about building a home for yourself in space, setting up a comforting nook for yourself in a vessel drifting over the face of the newly liberated gas giant. Wishlist Young Suns on Steam Release date: November 3, 2026 Imagine a future that's… good? This strange concept is the heart of Young Suns, which tasks you with designing a spaceship home in the stars in orbit around Jupiter, a newly liberated planet with a bright future ahead of it. Build your dreams space-home, explore the environs of our solar system's largest planet, and grow deeply attached to the game's cast of Jupiterians when it hits on November 3. Wishlist it on Steam . title: Escape From Playtime is a co-op survival horror where you play itsy-bitsy toy animals, and its playtest is taking signups now
summary: Many toy creatures will be harmed in the playing of this videogame.
body: There is, you must admit, something a bit disconcerting about children's toys. The sightless eyes, the static expressions—it all combines into a hollow unpersonhood that triggers some ancient, primeval fear in the low regions of your brain. Something that also doesn't help: the unslakeable lust for murder. Alright, that last part maybe does not apply to my childhood teddy bear, but it does apply to the nightmarish denizens of Escape From Playtime, which just announced it's accepting playtest sign-ups at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. Wishlist Escape From Playtime on Steam Release date: October 21, 2026 Fancy being scared? Fancy being scared and very, very small? Fancy being scared, very small, and accompanied by up to three of your pals? Escape From Playtime has just the thing for your very specific desires, friend: play as a tiny Smiling Critter navigating a haunted factory in a co-op survival horror whose playtest is taking signups now. Launching October 21 on Steam . You can also sign up for the playtest at EscapeFromPlaytime.com. title: Memory is the map in Wane, a roguelike where each biome is a corner of an archaeologist's fading mind
summary: An expedition unlike any other.
body: The best art is all about descending into someone's twisted psyche. It doesn't matter who, but the deeper we get into their very being, the better. Now buckle up and prepare for Wane, a roguelike where you quite literally navigate through the deconstructed mind of Declan Wayne, a fading archaeologist. We just revealed the game at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, and it looks like a corker—for any non-Brits, that means it looks really good. "I used to believe that memory makes a man," says Wayne as he narrates over the gorgeous trailer. "Now I know, it can unmake one, too." Wishlist Wane on Steam Release date: TBA This is the world premiere of Wane, a tactical roguelike where you descend into the depths of a man's memories. title: Command a legion of robots in factory builder Brave New Wonders, launching tomorrow
summary: Just write what you want them to do, easy as pie.
body: The best thing about machines is that they do exactly what you program them to do. The worst thing about machines is that they do exactly what you program them to do. In Brave New Wonders, releasing tomorrow, you'll build and automate a set of production lines with robots that you can write commands for. title: It's just you and your van in this upcoming open-world scavenging game
summary: Be wary of what lurks in the fog that rolls in at night.
body: Deep down, I know I want to abandon it all and live the life of a nomad. If I didn't have a family and friends to worry about, I'd pack some clothes into a van and drive off, moving from town to town and camping out in the woods. Unfortunately, I have responsibilities and no driver's license, so I can't head off just yet. I can, however, live out the fantasy in Hodka, a new game revealed at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. Hodka is an upcoming game from developer Flazm. In the reveal trailer, we see a dilapidated van cresting a hill next to some stone ruins. The scene is set: this is about you and your trusty home-on-wheels venturing through what remains of this troubled world. title: Yet another Pokémon-inspired game is popping off on Steam, with over 160,000 concurrent players for Aniimo
summary: Turns out people like collecting creatures.
body: Step aside Palworld, you are now merely the second most-played pastiche of the world's highest-grossing multimedia franchise on Steam. You've been overtaken by none other than Aniimo, the Genshin Impact-esque but non-gacha open world RPG, according to SteamDB . The numbers are climbing as I write this, with the game currently sitting at over 166,000 simultaneous players. That's a lot! For reference, it's sitting ahead of likes of Rust, Delta Force, and Slay the Spire 2, with only the mighty Bongo Cat and its lessers (Apex Legends, Dota 2, etc) making up the list of eight games with more players on Steam right now. At the very top is, as always, Counter-Strike 2. Just imagine the numbers it'd enjoy if it also had cute little creatures that only say their own name. When PC Gamer lead SEO editor Lauren Morton tried it, she wasn't wowed, saying "I can't find much about it that other creature collecting and gacha games aren't doing better"—though this was back in the closed beta from January. The game currently sits at a "Mostly Positive" rating on Steam, with many of the positive reviews praising its Pokémonishness and the negative reviews taking umbrage with its labyrinthine monetiza…

title: Co-op puzzle game We Were Here Tomorrow is out next month, so you've got time to practise your communication skills
summary: This time, we're in a strange facility.
body: As much as I enjoy multiplayer games, it's becoming more and more difficult to actually gather my friends for a session. We're growing up and have less time for games due to all our boring adult responsibilities, bleh. But give me a two player co-op game and I can normally convince my girlfriend to at least give it a go. Puzzle games are her favourite, so I reckon we'll be able to get properly stuck into We Were Here Tomorrow, the latest in the co-op puzzle series. And we only have to wait a month to play it. As we just revealed at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, We Were Here Tomorrow is launching October 20. It's the sixth game in the We Were Here series, all co-op puzzle games that involve you and a buddy teaming up to escape some sort of predicament. The games have taken us to castles, a deserted island, and now, a mysterious facility. title: Night Plane is a horror game designed to scare me, specifically, because I hate flying—and deer demons
summary: Prepare to save some souls.
body: I hate flying. Crammed into a tiny metal tube with 100s of other people, 1000s of feet in the air, unnaturally defying the will of God—it's awful. I don't know how flight attendants stay so calm and professional the entire time. At least in the real world they don't have to contend with shape-shifting demons like they do in Night Plane, the upcoming horror job sim from Liquid Static Studio. In a new trailer unveiled during the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, things get spooky real quick. A deer just stands there, menacingly staring at the flight attendant before they board the Plane Airlines plane, and we see a bloody handprint smeared on the emergency door. Wishlist Night Plane on Steam Release date: October 26, 2026 Attend to passengers while kicking shape-shifting demons off the plane, and be ready to save some souls if you crash land. Download Night Plane's Steam demo now and wishlist the game ahead of its October 26 release date. title: Videogame development sim Let's Build a Dungeon launches into early access February 11
summary: Do you have what it takes to make a good game?
body: Since you're reading this, chances are you've thought to yourself, "I bet I could make a better game than that." I know I have. Well, the chance for us to prove it will soon be upon us: MMORPG-maker Let's Build a Dungeon is launching into early access February 11, 2027. In Let's Build a Dungeon, you take control of a videogame studio making an MMORPG. It's part management simulator, part RPG maker. You'll be in charge of hiring devs, assigning work, even deciding if you'll make your workers crunch or not. Wishlist Let's Build a Dungeon on Steam Early access release date: February 11, 2027 Let's Build a Dungeon has you control a videogame studio and make the MMO it's developing. You've got to keep your players happy or they'll leave bad reviews and play something else. The game is launching into early access February 11, 2027. Wishlist it on Steam . title: In Falsus is a delightfully unforgiving rhythm game, though its best tracks are locked behind an unimpressive story
summary: In Falsus is part rhythm game, part visual novel, part… puzzle?
body: Critical Hit (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle. I'm almost certain my love for videogame music was the pipeline to becoming a chronic rhythm game enjoyer, combining two of my very favourite things (funky beats and button mashing), into some ridiculously good audio-visual experiences. It's still a genre that is woefully underrepresented on PC, though—sorry to all the Osu! enjoyers out there, I do not count myself among you—and as someone who primarily got started in arcades and continues to dwell in them, I've been yearning to bring that experience to my desktop. (Image credit: Lowiro) Luckily for me, In Falsus recently launched. It's from the same developer behind Arcaea, the mobile rhythm game that was very heavily inspired by Japanese arcade rhythm game Sound Voltex. That DNA carries through to In Falsus, with lightning-fast note streams and mouse-controlled skylane laser notes that require the kind of dexterity I still massively lack despite my many years served in the scene. summary: If you come for the king, you best not miss.
body: Once upon a time, if you fought the king and won, you became the new king. Thems were the rules. I'm not sure if those are still the rules—I live in the UK, so maybe even pondering this is treason—but I reckon these days you'd just get arrested. title: Iconic RPG Lufia is finally coming to PC, with the first two games in the series due next year
summary: Can you rise up and defeat the Sinistrals?
body: The wonderful world of Lufia is back, and this time, it's coming to PC. Just revealed in the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct was the world premiere of Lufia 1 & 2 The Sinistrals Saga—the iconic RPGs will be coming to Steam in 2027, marking the first time any games in the series will be officially available on PC. If you weren't around in the early '90s, you may not know about Lufia. The original, Lufia & the Fortress of Doom, came out in 1993 in Japan and North America—it skipped Europe entirely. Its opening is pretty unforgettable, as it instantly puts you in the shoes of the heroes of a legend, fighting four godlike enemies called the Sinistrals. It's a bold way to start a game. summary: Forget your putter, pack a taser.
body: How illegal can golf be? You stand on a neatly manicured lawn and whack a ball into a hole. Rinse and repeat up to 18 times and that's it, that's golf. Well, if you sneak onto a golf course with your mates at night and play a few holes, then it becomes Really Illegal Golf, a new game that just got its world premiere at the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct. Developed by Pushlab Games and published by No More Robots, Really Illegal Golf is a multiplayer game where you and your friends have to sneak around the city, playing golf in all the clubs you've been banned from. title: Mark Darrah, co-director of Dragon Age: Origins, has played Riven for 3 minutes and Factorio for 832 hours: 'If you want to know what kind of programmer someone would be, have them play Factorio'
summary: The BioWare veteran guides us through the games on his PC.
body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" Mark Darrah isn't much for reminiscing about games he played in his childhood, but he does recall being struck by his first encounter with Command & Conquer in his late teens: "The thing that probably affected me for the longest, the most deeply, was that you could do storytelling for real," Darrah says. "It had cinematic storytelling, at least for the time [and] I think the original Command & Conquer had a branching storyline." Two years after C&C's release, Darrah joined BioWare as a programmer, a role he'd perform for Baldur's Gate , Baldur's Gate 2 , Neverwinter Nights , and Jade Empire . But Darrah is best known as the executive producer of the Dragon Age series, as well as being co-director of Dragon Age: Origins and the director of Dragon Age 2 . In 2021, Darrah departed BioWare after 23 years at the studio. Today, he runs a game design consultancy business and moonlights as a YouT…

title: The latest co-op indie game to take over the internet is like one of my favourite board games, just with bombs
summary: This is teamwork at its most complicated.
body: They say if you give a monkey an infinite amount of time to randomly hit keys on a typewriter it will almost surely write Shakespeare's complete works, word for word. But what happens when you give three monkeys with restricted access to their senses a limited amount of time to defuse a bomb? It explodes, the bomb almost always explodes. This is the terrifying reality you must face in Bombanana, the new co-op bomb disposal game where you and three friends play as monkeys. The monkey part is fun, but not as crucial to the set up as the fact that one of you can't see, one can't hear, and one can't speak; that really throws a spanner in the works. It's like Team 3, the co-op building game which is also based on the three wise monkeys. (Image credit: TARK) I rounded up some friends and started as the monkey who can't see, who also happens to be the monkey that has to defuse the bomb. It's as tricky as you'd expect. None of us had any clue what was going on or how to communicate with one another. The person who had the instruction manual couldn't speak, the only person who could see what they were doing couldn't hear instructions or questions, and I couldn't see what the hell was going…

title: Hideo Kojima says he was 'shocked' after Sony cut ties with Physint over a Zoom call: 'Nothing could’ve prepared me for their decision to step away from the project'
summary: My first thought was, "What am I going to do with my studio?"
body: Sony's recent decision to cut ties with Kojima Productions's Physint is one of the more unexpected turns of 2026. Even with the industry's many struggles, and speculation that Death Stranding 2 didn't sell as well as Sony hoped, the PlayStation studio shutting the door on one of the industry's most famed and respected designers was a huge surprise. While Kojima Productions would eventually find a new publisher for Physint in Microsoft , it took a frantic three months of pitching for that happen. This is partly because Kojima himself was similarly blindsided by Sony's decision, as the veteran designer revealed in the first interview he's given since switching publishers. Speaking to IGN , Kojima revealed that in June, Sony contacted him saying they wanted to have a Zoom call, which he agreed to. It was during that call when Sony broke the bad news: "They said they can no longer fund development for Physint. I was shocked and I said 'What did you say?'" Kojima explained. "I couldn't quite process what they had said. I wasn't sure because I was in such shock." Kojima told IGN that he understood "the situation in the industry as a whole", with many studios being shut down and projects…

title: I urge you to check out this hidden object game where you play as the world's most helpful sniper
summary: Sniper Dan does whatever a sniper can.
body: On the list of activities that could feasibly be described as "wholesome", sniping is probably close to the bottom. While I enjoy ventilating skulls from improbably long distances in games like Battlefield 6 and Wardogs , it wouldn't be the first activity that I would consider sharing with the family. Which is why I so admire Sniper Dan 's attempt to turn sharpshooting into a positive experience on both sides of the scope. Developed by Autonauts creators Denki, Sniper Dan smashes together hidden-object games and first-person shooting, and in doing so produces a surprisingly effective symbiotic relationship. The loose premise sees Dan—a crack-shot armed with a hunting rifle and an entrepreneurial spirit, venture out into his local community hellbent upon projectile-based problem solving. Each mission is like a 3D, animated wimmelbilderbuch , scattered with dozens of people, animals, and inanimate objects which may or may not require bullet-based assistance. In play, Sniper Dan couldn't be simpler. You spy a problem, shoot the problem, and solve the problem. What makes it interesting is the wacky array of problems that require your assistance. title: Tokyo Walled City looks set to fill the Deus Ex-shaped hole in my life
summary: I am definitely asking for this.
body: It's been more than a decade since the last Deus Ex game, and it's unlikely we'll see another one any time soon. Yet while Adam Jensen's story remains frustratingly unfinished thanks to the cliffhanger ending of Deus Ex: Mankind Divided , the indie scene has offered fresh hope for fans of sneaking through moody cyberpunk cityscapes in the form of newly revealed immersive sim Tokyo Walled City . Unveiled at TGS 2026 , Tokyo Walled City is described by developer Grim Ronin as a "stealth action retro-cyberpunk immersive sim with survival horror and RPG elements". So, Deus Ex with scary bits, basically. You play as Reiko Kimura, a mercenary who is trapped in a dense, fortified district of Japan's capital, the name of which implies it is inspired by the Internet's favourite historic enclave Kowloon Walled City. Blade Runner is another clear inspiration, with the opening shot of the game's trailer showing a cityscape that directly references Blade Runner's "Coke billboard" scene. The rest of the trailer offers a montage of all the classic immersive sim tropes. Vent crawling, disabling security cameras, hacking into computers, 0451, shooting out lights, leaning around corners. title: Over 10 years later, Gabe Newell's advice to devs still holds up
summary: There can be a fine line between a malicious hack and a legend.
body: In 2013, Valve head honcho Gabe Newell spoke to students at the LBJ School of Public Affairs in Austin about "Productivity, Economics, Political Institutions & The Future of Corporations." It was a much more interesting topic than that makes it sounds, and has been doing the rounds again thanks to being sliced up into shorts by the Webknower channel . One clip that's been going around is Newell's response to being asked about how easy it is for hackers to get into game worlds and do things the creators don't want them to do: "One of the biggest mistakes game developers make is to mistake hacking, or to mistake a genuinely entertaining action by a player as hacking. So the example game developers tell each other is when Lord British was killed during his first speech in Ultima Online they rolled the world back rather than recognizing that it was the coolest thing that had ever happened in Ultima Online." In the early singleplayer Ultima games, Lord British had huge amounts of hit points and other defenses to discourage players from attacking him, which of course made some of those players see it as a challenge.
